title: Choosing Friends with Care
note: You should befriend only those you have examined and found to have the marks given above. This chapter is on how to examine them.

couplets.plain: Nothing ruins you like making friends without looking into them. For those who hold to friendship, once made there is no leaving it.
couplets.pm: For those who love friendship and stand by it, there is no leaving a friend once made. So nothing brings ruin like befriending someone without examining his character and conduct. Friends have no “I” and “he” between them, so his blame and sin become yours, and you are ruined in both worlds.

links.quote: Nothing ruins you like making friends without looking into them
once made there is no leaving it

couplets.plain: Someone who makes a friend without looking and looking again ends in a sorrow that kills him.
couplets.pm: If you don’t test many times and in many ways that a person’s character and conduct are good before you befriend him, you bring on yourself, with no help from your enemies, the grief that ends in your death. Befriend a bad man and all his enmities fall on you, and they kill you.

links.quote: makes a friend without looking and looking again

couplets.plain: Know a person’s character, family, faults and the unfailing kin around them, then make them your friend.
couplets.pm: Examine someone’s character, birth, faults and unfailing kin, then befriend him. No one in the world is faultless, so if his faults can be borne, the friendship isn’t to be dropped. People bound to their kin stay bound to their friends too. If you have to leave him later the failing is yours, so know him first.

links.quote: Know a person’s character, family, faults and the unfailing kin around them
links.reason: Lays out what to weigh: character, family, faults and the kin around them.

couplets.plain: Someone well-born, who shrinks from blame upon himself: win his friendship, even if you have to pay for it.
couplets.pm: Win the friendship of someone born in a high family who fears the blame the world may put on him, even by giving something for it. His birth keeps him from doing wrong, and his fear of blame makes him bear your wrongs. Someone with both is rare, so buy his friendship.

links.reason: Shrinking from blame is what makes such a friend worth paying for.

couplets.plain: Choose with care friends who, when you go wrong, can speak until you weep, rebuke you, and make you see the right way.
couplets.pm: Examine and befriend those who can stop you, with words that bring grief, when you mean to go against the way of the world. They press you not to do it again if you have, and they can make you do it when you fail to. The way of the world is what people have always done.

links.quote: can speak until you weep, rebuke you
links.reason: Tells you to seek out as friends the very people who will rebuke you.

links.quote: Choose with care friends who, when you go wrong, can speak until you weep

couplets.plain: Even in ruin there is one benefit: it is a rod that measures your people to their full length.
couplets.pm: A person’s ruin is a rod that measures every one of his friends, so even it brings him a good understanding. In good times their limits don’t show. When ruin comes they act differently, and it marks them out. Having measured them, you keep only the fit, and that knowledge is the benefit.

links.quote: Even in ruin there is one benefit
links.reason: Finds one gain in ruin: it measures who your own people are.

links.quote: a rod that measures your people to their full length
links.reason: Ruin is the rod laid against each of your people to take their true length.

links.quote: a rod that measures your people

couplets.plain: What counts as gain for a person is to give up the friendship of fools and get clear of them.
couplets.pm: If you have befriended fools, your true gain is to drop the friendship and move away from them. Even with the friendship over, staying near them brings harm, so he says “get clear”. Once clear you not only escape harm but gain the right to happiness in both worlds, so he calls it gain.

links.quote: give up the friendship of fools

couplets.plain: Don’t think of things that make your spirit small. Don’t take the friendship of those who cut away your strength in trouble.
couplets.pm: Don’t think of doing what shrinks your spirit: tasks begun against those stronger than you, and tasks with no use. In the same way, don’t take the friendship of those who abandon you when trouble comes. They seemed a strength before and then fall away, so he says they cut your strength. Take them, and you are surely ruined.

links.quote: those who cut away your strength in trouble
links.reason: Warns off those who cut away your strength the moment you are in trouble.

couplets.plain: The friendship of those who desert you in your ruin burns the heart, even if you think of it when death is upon you.
couplets.pm: The friendship of those who leave someone in his ruin burns the mind of anyone who recalls it, even at the hour Death comes to kill them. The mere thought is crueller than Death, even to someone unconnected. Such is friendship made with desertion in mind. Others read it as: when the ruin he made kills him, the memory burns worse than the ruin.

links.quote: burns the heart, even if you think of it when death is upon you

couplets.plain: Cling to the friendship of the spotless. Give something if you must, and leave the friendship of those who don’t fit.
couplets.pm: Cultivate the friendship of those who are in accord with the world and faultless. If you have unknowingly befriended those out of accord with it, give them what they ask and get free. The first brings joy in both worlds, and the second only sorrow, so buy your way out.

links.quote: Cling to the friendship of the spotless
links.reason: Urges holding to the spotless and leaving those who don’t fit, whatever that costs.

links.quote: Give something if you must, and leave the friendship of those who don’t fit
